Usage:
  agent-device scroll <direction|top|bottom> [amount] [--until <selector>] [--max-passes <n>] [--pixels <n>] [--duration-ms <ms>] [--settle]

Scroll in a direction, or toward the top/bottom edge of scrollable content. The until input scrolls to an off-screen selector in one command. The optional amount is the finger-path fraction of the viewport axis, honored up to 0.8 of it; directional scrolls reduce release momentum, while app scroll physics determine the final content offset. A visible keyboard shortens the swiped band instead of being dismissed; when too little is left, the command refuses with scroll_keyboard_occludes_surface. A directional scroll also reports the movement it observed as movement: moved, at-edge, unchanged, or unobserved when the two reads could not back a claim either way; an unchanged surface inside a container that still hides content in that direction refuses with scroll_no_progress rather than repeating the requested distance. The movement field is absent where a tier verifies per pass (top/bottom, until), where the runtime cannot read a screen, where a settle observation or a replay already owns that observation, or where the operator opted out of it. A caller that verifies the screen by polling can add --no-post-gesture-stabilization. The scroll then returns right after its gesture, with no movement field and no scroll_no_progress refusal, and the next read skips the stabilization wait. With --settle the settle observation already reports the outcome, and the option removes the same wait from its first capture.

Command flags:
  --duration-ms <ms>          Scroll: pace the gesture over this duration when supported
  --pixels <n>                Scroll: explicit gesture distance in pixels
  --until <selector>          Scroll: repeat passes until the selector is visible on screen
  --max-passes <n>            Scroll --until: maximum gestures
  --settle                    After the action, wait for the UI to go quiet and return the settled diff vs the pre-action tree in the same response (best-effort; never fails the action)
  --settle-quiet <ms>         Settle: quiet window the UI must hold to count as settled (default 500ms; 300ms when the settled tree comes from the iOS simulator snapshot bridge). On iOS, a broad screen replacement such as a modal dismissal is confirmed for at least 1500ms whatever window is asked for, within the --timeout settle deadline; a replacement from a screen the pre-action capture read as presenting nothing, such as a tab switch, gets no 1500ms confirmation and keeps the asked window
  --no-post-gesture-stabilization  Scroll, swipe, gesture swipe, open: skip the movement check and the stabilization wait that follow a gesture, and on a local iOS simulator the first-screen wait after an app launch; use it only when your own polling verifies the screen
  --timeout <ms>              Boot/Open/Prepare: startup budget covering the device boot (and runner preparation for prepare). Replay/Snapshot/Test: maximum wall-clock time for the command or attempt. With --settle: the settle-wait deadline (default 10s)
